axes.model_access:
**Ships its own compiled inference engine (MLCEngine)** — not a service calling an external model; it compiles models into native executables for the target platform
(the official positioning: "Universal LLM Deployment Engine with ML Compilation"). On the model side it takes the safetensors family
(the HF-weights-compile route), a different root from llama.cpp's pre-quantized GGUF route.
axes.runtime:
A **compile-and-deploy CLI/library** (pip mlc-llm / the mlc_llm command); the platform matrix is its headline surface:
NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPUs (CUDA/Vulkan/ROCm/OpenCL), Apple Metal (incl. iOS/iPadOS),
web browsers (WebGPU+WASM, the sister project WebLLM), Android (OpenCL) — the README platform table marks cell by cell.
GitHub mlc-ai/mlc-llm Apache-2.0 23,284 stars, pushed 2026-10-30 (API verified);
**GitHub releases nominally stop at v0.20.0 (dev tag v0.26.dev0) — the release line is on PyPI (the mlc-llm package)**.
axes.local_files:
Reads and writes local files — model weights (compiled artifacts cached locally), compile-config JSON; the REST server runs on a local port.
The compile step itself produces platform-specific artifacts (its operational difference from "download-and-run" runners).
axes.background: The REST server is a persistent local process (OpenAI-compatible API); no persistent cloud surface — purely local/self-hosted.
axes.tools:
Not an agent-tool surface — its "tools" are the command line and the API: the mlc_llm generate/generate-config/compile
subcommands + MLCEngine's **OpenAI-compatible REST API** (REST server/python/javascript/iOS/Android
backed by the same engine and same compiler — README wording).
axes.context:
No cross-session memory (it is an inference-serving surface) — context length follows the compile-time model config and runtime parameters;
conversation state is carried by the client, the server stores no sessions.
axes.permissions: Local runs are unauthenticated by default (REST server on a local port); the permission surface = local files and GPU access. No cloud account, no telemetry disclosure surface.
axes.fit:
Fits: "one engine, multi-platform deployment" — especially mobile (iOS/Android native Metal/OpenCL) and browser (WebLLM)
ends that llama.cpp/Ollama do not cover; an engineering route that trades compile-time optimization for runtime performance.
Does not fit: the convenience route of GGUF download-and-run (llama.cpp/Ollama); users who do not want to touch a compile step.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/runner/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/runner/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The current PyPI version number and upload date (pypi.org measured 000 direct and unreachable; per snapshot discipline no unverified numbers are recorded)
- The complete supported-model list (the docs have a list; not enumerated item by item)
- How compiled artifacts are distributed per platform (precompiled vs user-compiled boundary; the docs wording not verified item by item)
related: Contrast: Ollama is a productized GGUF pull-and-run wrapper; MLC is a compile-and-deploy engine, and its end coverage (phones/browsers) is what Ollama lacks.
Two roots contrasted: llama.cpp runs pre-quantized GGUF directly; MLC compiles safetensors into platform-native code.

Boundary contrast: a cloud chat entry (data on their side) vs a local compile-and-deploy engine (data never leaves the machine) — the OpenAI-compatible API makes them interchangeable for clients, while the data boundaries are completely different.
